```
Review by Emmett Watkins Jr.  PRO

The Odyssey  2026
⭐⭐⭐⭐½
Watched 30 Aug 2026

This movie has just about all the things I like in movies.

A cast full of incredible actors that is so stacked that even the most obscure, minor characters are played by folks I know as leads in other movies. Plus, every one of the most known names here get a scene or two that seems specifically designed to be the clip played at the Oscars when one of them get nominated for Best Supporting Actor. It feels like the Smash bros of actors I like from other stuff, from the A listers to the more obscure character actors. Everyone gets a chance to shine, and with a runtime this long, everyone has the space, too.
```

The movie is just sequence after sequence that made me say to myself "how the fuck did they do that". Every expansive set or every ornate prop, looked like it was created by real people and existed in physical space. Every chaotic shot with seemingly hundreds of extras on screen and every time a scene had live animals as a major element I sat with my mouth metaphorically agape at the fact that real people had to coordinate that chaos in a way to make it actual look chaotic, or people had to film with those live animals despite the actual chaos they would add to a real film set. My jaw only hit the floor so frequently because I know just enough about filmmaking to not take for granted when a film is made like this. There are certain scenes where computer generated images are required, but an impressive amount of what was on screen was real. Even the computer assisted parts are injected with so much inspired intention that they impressed in much the same way the rest of the film did. It’s cool to be reminded of what can be achieved when enough incredibly talented people combine their powers to make something beautiful.

The story and writing of this movie manages to feel modern without losing that epic, poetic sense of the original tale. Plus, perhaps because this is my first time experiencing the entire story from top to bottom, I finally understood what the story was thematically about. I don’t think I was ever assigned, over all the times I’ve interacted with The Odyssey in college and high school, to read the entire thing. That is because, unless I took a class dedicated to only this text, reading the entire thing would take too long for any class. But now that I have consumed even this abbreviated form of the story, I feel I appreciate it so much more. I found the individual moments of the story entertaining, and this film portrays those moments as thrilling as they felt on the page, if not moreso, but those moments didn’t carry much thematic weight originally. The way this story is paced, the way these performances jump off the screen, and again, the way the sometimes dense ancient language is adapted for modern ears makes this tale hit me harder than I could have imagined. As someone who has seen Passion of the Christ, that movie also felt larger than life but mostly due to the hype of its release and the fervor fellow Christians made about it. This is one of the rare movies that felt biblical in the same way, but not due to the way the film is held up by viewers, but due purely to the film itself. The timelessness of the original tale may very well rub off on this movie to eventually make it a timeless classic as well someday.

I just really enjoyed this movie. Sure, I saw it very late, so the audience wasn’t as enthused as I was when the credits rolled. Sure, the only IMAX viewing was an hour away, and I had forgotten just how expensive this format is since it’s been so long since I sought out tickets for it. And there may even be some small moments in the movie where I could tell iconic moments of the original story were sped through for the sake of the pacing of the core film. But none of that stuff matters when the movie left me feeling as invigorated as it did. In some ways, both the narrative themes of the movie, and the quality of the film itself, are gleaming monuments to the miracle of the human spirit. In the same way that it feels impossible one man can make it through a literal punishment from the gods, it feels impossible that movies like this can still be made in a world where hyper capitalist mentalities and AI delusions of grandeur emphasize the ends over the means. Well, I hope this film stands as yet another enduring example of what can be done when you give a shit about the means. Long live cinema, but more importantly, long live art, and the people who choose to still make it.
